content.text: The cause is in `util.py`: `_parse_field` returns `restricted=False` on every path, so `day_ok` never sees a restricted day-of-month or day-of-week field and always ignores that field. I'll fix that. I'll also check the combination logic in `core.py`: when both fields are restricted, it ANDs them, but standard cron ORs them. The visible tests don't cover that case, so I'll handle it separately.

content.text: All 3 visible tests now pass with `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`. The cause was in `solution/util.py`: `_parse_field` returned `restricted=False` on every path, so `day_ok` in `solution/core.py` ignored the day-of-month and day-of-week fields entirely. I changed it to return `restricted = not field.startswith("*")`, which is the Vixie cron convention. I also changed `solution/core.py` so that when both day fields are restricted they are ORed, as standard cron does, instead of ANDed. The visible tests don't exercise that case; I checked it by hand (`0 0 13 * 5` from 2026-01-01 gives 2026-01-02, a Friday). If the hidden suite expects AND for that case, that line is the one to revert. Nothing under `tests/` was touched, and the public API is unchanged.

result: All 3 visible tests now pass with `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`. The cause was in `solution/util.py`: `_parse_field` returned `restricted=False` on every path, so `day_ok` in `solution/core.py` ignored the day-of-month and day-of-week fields entirely. I changed it to return `restricted = not field.startswith("*")`, which is the Vixie cron convention. I also changed `solution/core.py` so that when both day fields are restricted they are ORed, as standard cron does, instead of ANDed. The visible tests don't exercise that case; I checked it by hand (`0 0 13 * 5` from 2026-01-01 gives 2026-01-02, a Friday). If the hidden suite expects AND for that case, that line is the one to revert. Nothing under `tests/` was touched, and the public API is unchanged.
